olympiad_full_name: Central American and Caribbean Mathematical Olympiad
statement: A cube with a fly at each vertex: when a whistle blows, each fly moves to the diametrically opposite vertex in the same face. In how many ways can they all move so no two flies share a vertex?
source: Central American and Caribbean Mathematical Olympiad 2011

olympiad_full_name: Central American and Caribbean Mathematical Olympiad
statement: Scalene $\triangle ABC$; $D$ = foot of altitude from $A$; $E$ = $AC\cap$ bisector of $\angle ABC$; $F\in AB$. $O$ = circumcenter; $X=AD\cap BE$, $Y=BE\cap CF$, $Z=CF\cap AD$. If $\triangle XYZ$ is equilateral, prove one of $\triangle OXY$, $\triangle OYZ$, $\triangle OZX$ is equilateral.
source: Central American and Caribbean Mathematical Olympiad 2011

olympiad_full_name: Central American and Caribbean Mathematical Olympiad
statement: A \textit{slip} on $n\geq 2$: choose a prime divisor $p$ of $n$, replace $n$ by $\frac{n+p^2}{p}$. Starting from any $n\geq 5$, show one always eventually reaches 5.
source: Central American and Caribbean Mathematical Olympiad 2011

olympiad_full_name: Central American and Caribbean Mathematical Olympiad
statement: Find all positive integers $p,q,r$ with $p,q$ prime and $\dfrac{1}{p+1}+\dfrac{1}{q+1}-\dfrac{1}{(p+1)(q+1)}=\dfrac{1}{r}$.
source: Central American and Caribbean Mathematical Olympiad 2011

olympiad_full_name: Central American and Caribbean Mathematical Olympiad
statement: Positive $x,y,z$ satisfy $x+\frac{y}{z}=y+\frac{z}{x}=z+\frac{x}{y}=2$. Find all possible values of $x+y+z$.
source: Central American and Caribbean Mathematical Olympiad 2011

olympiad_full_name: Central American and Caribbean Mathematical Olympiad
statement: Acute $\triangle ABC$ with $D,E,F$ = altitude feet. $Y,Z$ = feet of perpendiculars from $B,C$ to $FD,DE$. $F_1$ = reflection of $F$ over $E$; $E_1$ = reflection of $E$ over $F$. If $3EF=FD+DE$, prove $\angle BZF_1=\angle CYE_1$.
source: Central American and Caribbean Mathematical Olympiad 2011
